Hi Amanda —

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to learn more about Acme Health's ingest and logging needs for the pilot. Quick recap and next steps from our side so we can make the security review efficient: 

1) PII scope: you mentioned that any PHI/PII elements in prompts should be minimized or redacted, but Acme will need confirmation about what we persist. Can you confirm the three data classes you consider PII for the pilot (e.g., patient name, MRN, SSN)?

2) Retention policy: you asked about token retention and logging windows. We retain request/response telemetry for 30 days by default for hosted customers; Dedicated/Private options allow custom retention policies. If you need 90/30/0 policies, please indicate preferred windows.

3) Logging / audit controls: we can provide per-request metadata (timestamp, model, route, request id) and redact full prompt content on request. Naomi (cc'd) is the best contact for where/how we surface audit logs and what’s included in the SOC2 summary.

4) Data residency & cloud providers: you asked whether data crosses regions or is processed in specific cloud regions. We can pin processing to a US region for the pilot. Naomi will confirm the supported regions and whether telemetry vendors are US-based.

5) Third-party subprocessors: telemetry, analytics, marketplace integrations — we maintain a canonical subprocessor list (attached) and a short summary of SOC2 scope. Please review the attached Subprocessors CSV and let us know any blockers.

Attachments: Acme_Security_Questionnaire_v3.pdf (your security form we started), subprocessors_table.csv, Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf

Hi Amanda / Marissa —

Quick answers to Amanda's questions and some items for procurement: 

1) Telemetry vendors: Our telemetry pipeline collects request-level metadata (request id, token counts, latency, model used) and is configured to NOT store full prompt text for hosted customers by default. For cases where customers request logging for troubleshooting we can enable prompt retention but that is an opt-in and visible in the tenant settings. The telemetry vendors we use for aggregated metrics (e.g., Datadog for metrics, S3 for archive) receive only aggregated/hashed identifiers; none receive unredacted prompt content unless the customer explicitly enables troubleshooting logs and grants access.

2) Marketplace and partner flows: Marketplace connectors are isolated — partners do not get direct access to customer prompts/outputs. Marketplace integrations that run on our hosted tier are subject to the same subprocessor controls; if a customer elects an integration that requires data sharing, we surface that in the UI and obtain consent. For Dedicated/Private deployments, customers control integration installation.

3) Cloud providers & residency: For hosted customers, processing occurs in the cloud region you select (we support us-west, us-east, eu-west). We can pin the pilot to US (us-west) and disable cross-region backups if required. All storage is encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+). KMS-backed encryption is available; keys can be customer-managed in Dedicated/Private.

4) Subprocessors: see attached subprocessors_table.csv — the key telemetry/analytics vendors are listed and include Datadog (metrics), S3-compatible storage providers, and a managed DB service for job/queue state. We maintain SOC2 attestations for our core infra providers; Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf attached includes scope.

5) Retention: By default 30 days for request/telemetry; prompt retention is 0 days unless enabled. We can offer bespoke retention windows on Dedicated/Private.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf, subprocessors_table.csv

If procurement needs an official attestation for any subprocessor, let me know which vendor and I’ll pull the hosted subprocessor contract IDs and attestations. Happy to hop on a 30-min call next week to walk procurement through the CSV.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Security & Privacy | Redwood Inference
